title: Finite Compact Non-Abelian Lattice Data and Wilson Holonomy

items.title: Finite non-Abelian lattice gauge data
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
items.statement:
Assume the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Fix the compact noncommutative finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$ supplied by the earlier non-Abelian gauge-data definition. Its Lie algebra is $\mathfrak g=T_eG$, with bracket induced by left-invariant smooth vector fields. Fix also a finite-dimensional complex vector space $W$, a positive-definite Hermitian form $h$ on $W$, and a specified smooth group homomorphism $\rho:G\to U(W,h)$, where $U(W,h)$ is the group of invertible complex-linear maps preserving $h$. Thus multiplication and inversion on $G$ are smooth, $G$ is compact in its manifold topology, and every $\rho(g)$ preserves $h$. Every finite power $G^S$ below has the product smooth-manifold structure, with charts given by products of charts of $G$; for $S=\varnothing$, set $G^S=\{()\}$ with its one-point smooth structure. No connection, principal bundle sector, action functional, or continuum theory is part of the lattice data below.

A **finite oriented lattice two-complex** is a finite set $\mathcal V$ of vertices, a finite set $\mathcal E^+$ containing one chosen orientation of each edge, an endpoint map $s,t:\mathcal E^+\to\mathcal V$, and a finite set $\mathcal F$ of faces. Each face $p\in\mathcal F$ is supplied with a based closed edge word $(e_1,\ldots,e_k)$ in the oriented edges $\mathcal E^+\sqcup\overline{\mathcal E^+}$, where the endpoint of each edge is the starting point of the next and the last endpoint is the first starting point. For the reverse orientation $\bar e$ of $e\in\mathcal E^+$, set $s(\bar e)=t(e)$ and $t(\bar e)=s(e)$.

A **link configuration** is a tuple $U=(U_e)_{e\in\mathcal E^+}\in G^{\mathcal E^+}$, with $U_{\bar e}:=U_e^{-1}$. The **holonomy of a face** $p=(e_1,\ldots,e_k)$ is the ordered product $U_p:=U_{e_1}\cdots U_{e_k}$ in traversal order, with the first traversed edge on the left. The vertex gauge group is $G^{\mathcal V}$ with coordinatewise multiplication; write $\mathbf e=(e)_{v\in\mathcal V}$ for its identity tuple. It acts by

$$
(h\cdot U)_e=h_{s(e)}U_eh_{t(e)}^{-1},\qquad h=(h_v)_{v\in\mathcal V}\in G^{\mathcal V}.
$$

Choose a normalized bi-invariant finite Radon Borel probability measure $\mu_G$ on $G$; explicitly, $\mu_G(G)=1$ and $\mu_G(gA)=\mu_G(Ag)=\mu_G(A)$ for every $g\in G$ and Borel $A\subseteq G$. The link measure is the finite product $\mu_G^{\mathcal E^+}$; for $\mathcal E^+=\varnothing$, this is the unit point mass on $G^{\varnothing}=\{()\}$. Empty sums are zero. For each face choose a continuous dimensionless function $\Phi_p:G\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $\Phi_p(gzg^{-1})=\Phi_p(z)$ and $\Phi_p(z^{-1})=\Phi_p(z)$. Define the dimensionless lattice action and its normalized expectation by

$$
S_\Lambda(U):=\sum_{p\in\mathcal F}\Phi_p(U_p),\qquad Z_\Lambda:=\int_{G^{\mathcal E^+}}e^{-S_\Lambda(U)}\,d\mu_G^{\mathcal E^+}(U),\qquad \langle O\rangle_\Lambda:=Z_\Lambda^{-1}\int_{G^{\mathcal E^+}}O(U)e^{-S_\Lambda(U)}\,d\mu_G^{\mathcal E^+}(U)
$$

for bounded measurable $O:G^{\mathcal E^+}\to\mathbb C$. The finite-volume **Gauss sector** is the closed subspace of $L^2(G^{\mathcal E^+},\mathbb P_\Lambda)$ consisting of measurable functions with finite integral of $|f|^2$, modulo equality $\mathbb P_\Lambda$-almost everywhere, whose equivalence classes are invariant under each element of $G^{\mathcal V}$. Here $\mathbb P_\Lambda$ is the normalized probability with density $Z_\Lambda^{-1}e^{-S_\Lambda}$ relative to product link measure. For $v\in\mathcal V$ and $X\in\mathfrak g$, let $X^{(v)}$ be the tangent vector at the identity of $G^{\mathcal V}$ with component $X$ at $v$ and zero at other vertices. If $\alpha(h,U)=h\cdot U$, define the infinitesimal **Gauss generator** on $C^\infty(G^{\mathcal E^+})$ by

$$
(D_{v,X}f)(U):=df_U\!\left(d\alpha_{(\mathbf e,U)}(X^{(v)},0)\right).
$$

The full Gauss sector uses invariance under every vertex gauge transformation; the infinitesimal equations $D_{v,X}f=0$ alone are not asserted to impose invariance under disconnected components of $G$. Link variables and the action are dimensionless. This finite mathematical regulator makes no continuum-limit or empirical claim.

items.title: Finite lattice gauge data define an invariant probability
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $\mathcal V,\mathcal E^+,\mathcal F$ be finite vertex, positively oriented edge, and face sets with endpoint maps $s,t$ and based closed face words in the oriented edges, using the reverse-edge convention and traversal-ordered holonomy from the finite lattice definition above. Use its product smooth structures and empty-product convention. Let $G$ be its compact finite-dimensional real Lie group, $\mu_G$ its normalized bi-invariant link probability, and $\Phi_p:G\to\mathbb R$ its continuous conjugation-invariant face actions. Then the vertex formulas $(h\cdot U)_e=h_{s(e)}U_eh_{t(e)}^{-1}$ define a smooth group action on $G^{\mathcal E^+}$. Each face holonomy transforms by conjugation at its base vertex. Consequently the product link measure and the Boltzmann weight $e^{-\sum_p\Phi_p(U_p)}$ are gauge invariant, and the partition function satisfies $0<Z_\Lambda<\infty$. Thus the normalized finite-lattice expectation is a well-defined gauge-invariant probability expectation. In $L^2$ of that probability, the subspace of classes invariant under each vertex gauge transformation is closed. The infinitesimal Gauss generators defined by differentiating this smooth action are well-defined as directional derivatives on smooth functions.

items.title: Wilson loop on a finite lattice
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and take finite oriented lattice data with finite vertex set $\mathcal V$, positively oriented edge set $\mathcal E^+$, endpoint maps $s,t$, compact group $G$, link variables $U_e$ for $e\in\mathcal E^+$, and vertex action $U_e\mapsto h_{s(e)}U_eh_{t(e)}^{-1}$. Write $\overline{\mathcal E^+}$ for the disjoint set of formal reverse edges, with endpoints interchanged, and set $U_{\bar e}=U_e^{-1}$. Fix a finite-dimensional complex vector space $W$ with positive-definite Hermitian form $h$ and a smooth group homomorphism $\rho:G\to U(W,h)$, where $U(W,h)$ is the group of invertible complex-linear maps preserving $h$; put $d=\dim_{\mathbb C}W\geq1$. A **based closed lattice loop** is a finite edge word $C=(e_1,\ldots,e_\ell)$ with each $e_i\in\mathcal E^+\sqcup\overline{\mathcal E^+}$, of integer length $\ell\geq0$, and a chosen base vertex $v_0$, such that consecutive endpoints match and, when $\ell>0$, the first and last endpoints are $v_0$; when $\ell=0$, the loop consists only of $v_0$. Its ordered holonomy is $U_C:=U_{e_1}\cdots U_{e_\ell}$, in traversal order with the first edge on the left; for $\ell=0$, set $U_C=e$. The reversed word is $C^{-1}=(\bar e_\ell,\ldots,\bar e_1)$. The **normalized Wilson loop** is

$$
W_\rho(C;U):=\frac{1}{d}\operatorname{Tr}_W\!\big(\rho(U_C)\big).
$$

The loop is dimensionless. Changing the base vertex by a cyclic rebase conjugates $U_C$ and leaves $W_\rho$ unchanged; reversing the loop gives $W_\rho(C^{-1};U)=\overline{W_\rho(C;U)}$. On a fixed finite lattice with a specified finite product Haar probability and bounded action, $\langle W_\rho(C)\rangle_\Lambda$ is the ordinary normalized finite-dimensional integral. No renormalized continuum Wilson loop or continuum limit is defined here.

items.title: Wilson loop is invariant under vertex gauge transformations
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $G$ be a group and let $(W,q)$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hermitian inner-product space. Define $U(W,q):=\{T\in\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbb C}(W):q(Tu,Tv)=q(u,v)\text{ for all }u,v\in W\}$, and let $\rho:G\to U(W,q)$ be a group homomorphism, with $d=\dim_{\mathbb C}W\geq1$. Let a finite oriented graph have vertices $\mathcal V$ and one chosen orientation $\mathcal E^+$ for each edge; for $e\in\mathcal E^+$ write $s(e),t(e)$ for its source and target. A link configuration assigns $U_e\in G$ to each $e\in\mathcal E^+$ and sets $U_{\bar e}=U_e^{-1}$. A based closed edge word $C=(e_1,\ldots,e_\ell)$ has length $\ell\geq0$, consecutive endpoints match, and when $\ell>0$ it starts and ends at a chosen vertex $v_0$; for $\ell=0$ it consists only of $v_0$. Put $U_C:=U_{e_1}\cdots U_{e_\ell}$ in traversal order, with the empty product equal to the identity, and put $W_\rho(C;U):=d^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}_W(\rho(U_C))$. For every vertex tuple $k\in G^{\mathcal V}$ acting by $(k\cdot U)_e=k_{s(e)}U_ek_{t(e)}^{-1}$, one has $U_C(k\cdot U)=k_{v_0}U_C(U)k_{v_0}^{-1}$. Thus the normalized trace is gauge invariant and unchanged when the based word is cyclically rotated; for $\ell>0$ reversal is $C^{-1}=(\bar e_\ell,\ldots,\bar e_1)$, while the empty word reverses to itself, and $W_\rho(C^{-1};U)=\overline{W_\rho(C;U)}$.

items.title: Finite SU(2) Wilson plaquette measure
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Use the matrix group $G_2=SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_2,\ \det U=1\}$ with matrix multiplication and the embedded smooth-manifold structure on $M_2(\mathbb C)\cong\mathbb R^8$ used for special unitary matrix groups. Its defining representation is the identity smooth homomorphism $\rho_2(U)=U$ on $W=\mathbb C^2$ with positive-definite Hermitian form $h(v,w)=v^*w$. In real coordinates every element has the form

$$
U(x)=\begin{pmatrix}x_0+ix_3&x_2+ix_1\\-x_2+ix_1&x_0-ix_3\end{pmatrix},\qquad x\in S^3:=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\textstyle\sum_{j=0}^3x_j^2=1\}.
$$

Let $\sigma_3$ be the induced round surface-area measure on $S^3$, whose total area is $2\pi^2$, and let $\mu_2$ be the pushforward of $\sigma_3/(2\pi^2)$ under $x\mapsto U(x)$. In spherical coordinates $x_0=\cos\theta$, $(x_1,x_2,x_3)=\sin\theta\,n$, $0\leq\theta\leq\pi$, $n\in S^2$, its coordinate density is $d\mu_2=(2/\pi)\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\,d\omega_2(n)$, where $n=(\sin\varphi\cos\psi,\sin\varphi\sin\psi,\cos\varphi)$ and $d\omega_2=(1/(4\pi))\sin\varphi\,d\varphi\,d\psi$ for $0\leq\varphi\leq\pi$, $0\leq\psi<2\pi$. Define the real class function $\tau(U):=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)=x_0$.

For each oriented face $p$, let $U_p$ be the product of its link matrices in boundary traversal order, using inverse matrices on reverse edges. For dimensionless $\beta\geq0$, define the pure-gauge Wilson plaquette action on any finite oriented lattice by

$$
S_\beta(U):=\beta\sum_{p}\bigl(1-\tau(U_p)\bigr),\qquad \beta=\frac{4}{g_0^2}
$$

when a dimensionless bare coupling $g_0>0$ is used. The finite link measure is the product of $\mu_2$ over positively oriented edges, and its normalized expectation is the finite product integral with density proportional to $e^{-S_\beta}$. The one-plaquette normalizing factor and one-plaquette probability are

$$
z_\beta:=\int_{G_2}e^{\beta\tau(U)}\,d\mu_2(U),\qquad d\nu_\beta(U):=z_\beta^{-1}e^{\beta\tau(U)}d\mu_2(U).
$$

Since $\tau(U)=x_0\in[-1,1]$, every $\beta\geq0$ gives $e^{-\beta}\leq z_\beta\leq e^\beta$; hence $z_\beta$ is finite and positive and $\nu_\beta$ is a normalized probability measure.

This defines only a finite-lattice mathematical measure; it does not define an infinite-volume or continuum expectation.

items.title: Independent plaquette variables on a finite planar rectangle
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $G$ be a group with a compact topology for which multiplication and inversion are continuous; compact means every open cover has a finite subcover. Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability, so $\mu(G)=1$, satisfying $\mu(hA)=\mu(Ah)=\mu(A)$ for every $h\in G$ and Borel $A\subseteq G$. Write $\mathcal B(G)$ for its Borel sigma-algebra and $m(x,y)=xy$. Require $m^{-1}(A)\in\mathcal B(G)\otimes\mathcal B(G)$ for every $A\in\mathcal B(G)$. Inversion is Borel measurable by continuity. In particular, this joint-measurability condition holds for the compact finite-dimensional real Lie groups supplied by the non-Abelian gauge datum. For positive integers $M,N$, let $\Lambda_{M,N}$ have vertices $(i,j)$ with $0\leq i\leq M$ and $0\leq j\leq N$, east-oriented horizontal edges $h_{i,j}:(i,j)\to(i+1,j)$ for $0\leq i<M$, $0\leq j\leq N$, north-oriented vertical edges $v_{i,j}:(i,j)\to(i,j+1)$ for $0\leq i\leq M$, $0\leq j<N$, and faces $p_{i,j}$ for $0\leq i<M$, $0\leq j<N$. The face $p_{i,j}$ has counterclockwise boundary word $(h_{i,j},v_{i+1,j},\bar h_{i,j+1},\bar v_{i,j})$, started at its lower-left vertex; multiply its link elements in traversal order, with the first factor on the left. Let $G^{\mathcal V}$ act on positively oriented link variables by $(g\cdot U)_e=g_{s(e)}U_eg_{t(e)}^{-1}$. Use the product Haar measure $\mu^{\mathcal E^+}$ on links and free boundary edges. Give each face a positive continuous weight $w_{i,j}:G\to(0,\infty)$ satisfying $w_{i,j}(gzg^{-1})=w_{i,j}(z)$ and $w_{i,j}(g^{-1})=w_{i,j}(g)$ for all $g,z\in G$, and normalize the density proportional to $\prod_{i,j}w_{i,j}(U_{p_{i,j}})$ relative to this link measure. For any chosen column $a\in\{0,\ldots,M\}$, fixing the gauge factor at $(a,0)$ to the identity gives a unique representative with every horizontal edge and every vertical edge in column $a$ equal to the identity. Write $V_{i,j}$ for the vertical link in this representative and set $P_{i,j}:=V_{i+1,j}V_{i,j}^{-1}$. The plaquette variables $(P_{i,j})$ are independent, and $P_{i,j}$ has probability

$$
d\nu_{i,j}(g)=\frac{w_{i,j}(g)}{\int_Gw_{i,j}(z)\,d\mu(z)}\,d\mu(g).
$$

This is a finite planar lattice statement with no periodic identifications or continuum limit.

items.title: SU(2) one-plaquette matrix average at strong coupling
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and use the finite $SU(2)$ Wilson plaquette measure for $\beta>0$: $\mu_2$ is the pushforward of normalized round area $\sigma_3/(2\pi^2)$ on $S^3$ under the displayed matrix-coordinate map $x\mapsto U(x)$, and $\tau(U)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)$. Put

$$
I_0(\beta):=\int_{SU(2)}e^{\beta\tau(U)}d\mu_2(U),\qquad I_1(\beta):=\int_{SU(2)}\tau(U)e^{\beta\tau(U)}d\mu_2(U),\qquad \lambda(\beta):=I_1(\beta)/I_0(\beta).
$$

Then $\mu_2$ is a normalized bi-invariant Borel probability, $I_0(\beta)>0$, $0<\lambda(\beta)<1$, and the defining-representation matrix expectation is

$$
\int_{SU(2)}U\,d\nu_\beta(U)=\lambda(\beta)I_2.
$$

As $\beta\downarrow0$, $\lambda(\beta)=\beta/4+O(\beta^3)$. The parameter $\beta$ and the one-plaquette expectation are dimensionless.

items.title: Exact finite-lattice SU(2) Wilson area law in two dimensions
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M,N\geq1$ be integers and use the finite $M$-by-$N$ square lattice with free boundary (no periodic identifications and all boundary links retained). Its vertices are $(i,j)$ for $0\leq i\leq M$, $0\leq j\leq N$; its positively oriented edges are eastward $h_{i,j}:(i,j)\to(i+1,j)$ for $0\leq i<M$, $0\leq j\leq N$, and northward $v_{i,j}:(i,j)\to(i,j+1)$ for $0\leq i\leq M$, $0\leq j<N$; and its faces $p_{i,j}$ for $0\leq i<M$, $0\leq j<N$ have counterclockwise boundary words $(h_{i,j},v_{i+1,j},\bar h_{i,j+1},\bar v_{i,j})$. Use the matrix group $SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_2,\det U=1\}$ with matrix multiplication and its identity defining representation. In real coordinates its elements are

$$
U(x)=\begin{pmatrix}x_0+ix_3&x_2+ix_1\\-x_2+ix_1&x_0-ix_3\end{pmatrix},\qquad x\in S^3:=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\textstyle\sum_{j=0}^3x_j^2=1\}.
$$

Let $\sigma_3$ be the induced round surface-area measure on $S^3$, with total area $2\pi^2$, and let $\mu_2$ be the pushforward of $\sigma_3/(2\pi^2)$ under this map. Each positively oriented edge carries one link matrix; reverse links use inverses. For each face $p$, $U_p$ is the product of its boundary links in traversal order; for a loop $C$, $U_C$ is the analogous ordered edge product. Use the Wilson action $S_\beta(U)=\beta\sum_p(1-\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2 U_p)$ and normalized loop $W(C)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2 U_C$. Let $\beta=4/g_0^2$ for dimensionless $g_0>0$, and restrict to the explicit strong-coupling window $0<\beta\leq1$ (equivalently $g_0^2\geq4$). For any axis-aligned rectangle contained in the lattice with corners $(a,c)$ and $(b,d)$, where $0\leq a<b\leq M$ and $0\leq c<d\leq N$, let $C_{a,b;c,d}$ be its boundary traversed counterclockwise from $(a,c)$. Its area in plaquette units is $A=(b-a)(d-c)$. Define $Z(SU(2)):=\{z\in SU(2):zU=Uz\text{ for every }U\in SU(2)\}$ and $\chi:Z(SU(2))\to\{\pm1\}$ by $z=\chi(z)I_2$. Then $Z(SU(2))=\{I_2,-I_2\}$ and the defining representation has the nontrivial central character $\chi(I_2)=1$, $\chi(-I_2)=-1$. Put

$$
\lambda(\beta):=\frac{\int_{SU(2)}\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)e^{\beta\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)/2}\,d\mu_2(U)}{\int_{SU(2)}e^{\beta\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)/2}\,d\mu_2(U)},
$$

where $\tau(U)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)$. Then $0<\lambda(\beta)<1$ and the exact finite-lattice expectation is

$$
\langle W(C_{a,b;c,d})\rangle_\beta=\lambda(\beta)^A=\exp\!\bigl(-\sigma_{\rm lat}(\beta)A\bigr),\qquad \sigma_{\rm lat}(\beta):=-\log\lambda(\beta)>0.
$$

The parameter $\beta$ and the lattice string tension $\sigma_{\rm lat}$ are dimensionless. The identity holds for every finite container and every stated rectangle; no infinite-area, infinite-volume, or continuum limit is taken, and no continuum confinement or mass-gap claim follows.

items.title: One-plaquette SU(2) Wilson average
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For one square face with free boundary in the finite $SU(2)$ Wilson model at $0<\beta\leq1$, take the loop to follow the positively oriented face boundary counterclockwise from its lower-left corner. Let $U_{\partial\square}$ be the ordered product of the face's link matrices in traversal order, using inverse matrices on reverse edges, and set $W(\partial\square):=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2(U_{\partial\square})$. Use $\mu_2$, the normalized pushforward of round $S^3$ surface area under the matrix-coordinate map in the finite $SU(2)$ plaquette-measure definition, and $\tau(U)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2U$. The normalized plaquette holonomy has law $d\nu_\beta(U)=z_\beta^{-1}e^{\beta\tau(U)}d\mu_2(U)$, where $z_\beta=\int e^{\beta\tau}d\mu_2$. The Wilson action partition factor is $Z_\square=e^{-\beta}z_\beta$, and this normalized fundamental loop has expectation $\langle W(\partial\square)\rangle_\beta=\lambda(\beta)$, where $\lambda(\beta)=\int\tau e^{\beta\tau}d\mu_2/z_\beta=\beta/4+O(\beta^3)$ as $\beta\downarrow0$.

items.title: Two-plaquette SU(2) rectangle
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Take a free-boundary $SU(2)$ square lattice containing a rectangle two plaquettes wide and one plaquette high, and let $C$ follow its oriented face boundary counterclockwise from the lower-left corner. Its loop holonomy $U_C$ is the ordered link product, using inverse matrices on reverse edges, and the defining normalized Wilson loop is $W(C):=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2(U_C)$. For $0<\beta\leq1$, the enclosed area is $A=2$ plaquettes, so the exact finite-lattice expectation is $\langle W(C)\rangle_\beta=\lambda(\beta)^2=\beta^2/16+O(\beta^4)$ as $\beta\downarrow0$, where

$$
\lambda(\beta):=\frac{\int_{SU(2)}\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)e^{\beta\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)/2}\,d\mu_2(U)}{\int_{SU(2)}e^{\beta\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)/2}\,d\mu_2(U)}
$$

is the finite one-plaquette coefficient for $\mu_2$, the normalized pushforward of round $S^3$ surface area under the matrix-coordinate map in the finite $SU(2)$ plaquette-measure definition.
